$comment: The operator policy's alarm scope (control.alarm_sources, control.alarm_max_severity), driven through BOTH runtimes: tests/unit/test_alarm_scope.py and packages/server-node/test/alarm-scope.test.mjs call checkAlarmScope / check_alarm_scope on each `input` and assert `expect`. `source` and `sources` are canonical node IDs (resolved); `sources` null and `max_severity` null mean not configured. `error` is why the condition's SourceNode or Severity could not be read, which refuses: an alarm whose scope cannot be checked is not acknowledged on the policy's behalf.

cases.name: the source is not listed
cases.expect: Condition ns=1;i=1001 is raised by ns=1;s=Temperature, which is not in the operator policy's alarm_sources. Nothing was acknowledged or changed.

cases.name: no source with sources configured
cases.expect: Condition ns=1;i=1001 is raised by an unknown source, which is not in the operator policy's alarm_sources. Nothing was acknowledged or changed.

cases.name: too severe
cases.expect: Condition ns=1;i=1001 has severity 700, above the operator policy's alarm_max_severity of 500, so a person has to handle it. Nothing was acknowledged or changed.

cases.name: severity at the limit is allowed
an unknown severity with a limit configured
cases.expect: Condition ns=1;i=1001 has severity unknown, above the operator policy's alarm_max_severity of 500, so a person has to handle it. Nothing was acknowledged or changed.

cases.name: a read error refuses
cases.expect: Condition ns=1;i=1001 could not be checked against the operator policy's alarm scope (SourceNode: BadNoMatch), so nothing was acknowledged or changed.

cases.name: the source is checked before the severity
cases.expect: Condition ns=1;i=1001 is raised by ns=1;s=Temperature, which is not in the operator policy's alarm_sources. Nothing was acknowledged or changed.
